name: Direct Sockets (TCP, UDP)
plain: Raw TCP and UDP sockets from a page, for installed isolated apps only.
meaning: Lets an installed Isolated Web App open arbitrary TCP and UDP connections and servers. Not available to normal websites because it would bypass same-origin and CORS protections.

web.api: new TCPSocket(host, port); new UDPSocket(); new TCPServerSocket(); policies direct-sockets, direct-sockets-private

access.prompt_ui: Only inside Isolated Web Apps (signed bundles); IWA install prompt; permission policy direct-sockets, plus direct-sockets-private for LAN ranges.
steps: User installs an Isolated Web App

limits.headline: Can open raw network connections only inside signed, installed apps, never on normal sites
limits.user_action: An organization installs a signed Isolated Web App on your computer
can: Open direct two way connections to other computers and devices
Run small servers inside the installed app
Reach local network devices if the app also has the extra network permission
cannot: Work on iPhone, Firefox or Safari
Work on Chrome for Android or Samsung Internet
Run without a signed bundle and an install by you or your IT team
limits.differs: Only desktop Chromium has it, and only for signed Isolated Web Apps. Other browsers and phones do not.

story.what_it_is: Installed special web apps can open raw network connections, like a desktop program.

marketing.name: Direct Sockets API
marketing.pitch: A way for isolated apps to talk to devices and servers over plain TCP and UDP, as desktop apps can.

story.for_you: Only a few packaged apps can use this, and you install them first. You may see a permission step. If you do not install the app, nothing happens.
story.for_makers: Makers get a way to bring remote desktop tools, game servers and device managers to the web without a native app. It needs strong trust, so it is limited to signed and installed apps.

use_cases.example: A remote desktop app in a browser window connects to office computers over their own protocol, with no plugin installed.
A web version of a game server list queries game servers directly over UDP to show player counts and ping.
A web based terminal connects to a device over raw network ports, so a developer can manage hardware from a browser app.
A web app sets up a smart light or printer by talking to its local network service directly.
A web app for music studios sends live note data to other devices on the same network using raw network messages.
A web based network tool scans office devices to find which are online, which is only allowed in an installed trusted app.
A coding class tool lets students try network programs in a browser sandbox with real connections.

abuse: Would enable malware-like network access if opened to the web

history.change: Direct Sockets for Isolated Web Apps
